narrative.overview:
Moon Code is a focused developer workbench: calm enough for long sessions, dense enough to keep project state close, and explicit enough that an Agent action never feels mysterious. The current homepage establishes a cool, near-white canvas with translucent workspace layers, one blue action accent, and compact status surfaces. The system should feel like a well-calibrated instrument panel rather than a marketing page.

The visual language serves 高效、清晰、可靠. Preserve the existing desktop-tool familiarity while tightening anything that competes with the task.
keyCharacteristics: Cool light workbench surfaces with a restrained blue primary.
Compact, familiar controls with 7–12px corner radii.
Layered panels and dividers establish hierarchy.
Motion is short, state-driven, and reduced when requested.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Moon Blue is for action, selection, focus, links, and information state.

rules.name: The State-Truth Rule
rules.body: If a value is unavailable, show an unavailable state and no proportional fill.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: Persistent interface copy is at least 11px and must meet a 4.5:1 contrast target where it carries meaning.

rules.name: The Layered-Not-Glossy Rule
rules.body: Use a neutral surface change or hairline before reaching for blur or shadow.

rules.name: The Object-Before-State Rule
rules.body: Project rows always retain the folder icon; never replace it with a disclosure caret solely to communicate expanded or collapsed state.

dos: Do use Moon Blue only for action, selection, focus, links, and information state.
Do preserve the cool light workbench field and white transcript/composer surfaces as the homepage baseline.
Do keep persistent UI text at 11px or larger and verify 4.5:1 contrast for meaningful copy.
Do retain the folder icon on every project row, whether expanded or collapsed.
donts: Don't make the product feel over-gamified or like a marketing landing page.
Don't stack information without hierarchy; empty panels should not look like broken dashboards.
Don't pair a 1px border with a 16px+ diffuse shadow on the same card or popover.
Don't render a full progress track when usage/context data is unavailable.
Don't replace a project folder icon with a disclosure caret solely to show expansion state.
